fixes.explanation: Servant is a fair guess for a man working under a king, friend, but it's not the word. Joseph says God has made him a father to Pharaoh (Genesis 45:8). Then he keeps going: lord of all Pharaoh's household and ruler over all the land of Egypt. That's a long way up from servant.

Prison is a real part of Joseph's story (Genesis 39:20), but he leaves it out of this message. What he tells them to pass along is “all my splendor in Egypt and everything you have seen.” (Genesis 45:13). I think he's got good news on his mind for his dad, and he wants that part heard first.

Pharaoh's dreams were a big moment, I'll give you that. Joseph already explained them back in Genesis 41:25, so that part is told. This time the brothers carry a different report home: his splendor in Egypt, along with everything they've seen (Genesis 45:13). That's the thing he wants Jacob to hear.

Brothers showing up at a ruler's door could sound like trouble, but the text says Pharaoh and his servants were pleased (Genesis 45:16). Pharaoh was the king of Egypt, and he tells Joseph to have the family bring their father and come back (Genesis 45:18). He even promises them the best of the land of Egypt. So the answer is True, and it's a warm welcome.
